standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma that CM morphisms of finite presentation have equidimensional fibres of constant local dimension after shrinking (Morphisms, flat-finite-presentation-CM-fibres-relative-dimension) and the dimension formula for morphisms of given relative dimension (Morphisms, rel-dimension-dimension); cited inputs with the reduction written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Shrink X to an open neighbourhood of x.
Obtain the constant fibre dimension d from the CM-fibres relative dimension lemma.
Conclude the pointwise dimension formula from the relative-dimension formula for flat maps.

proof_roadmap.step: Shrink and pin the constant fibre dimension via the CM-fibres lemma.
Apply the dimension formula for morphisms of relative dimension d.

difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X -> Y of locally Noetherian schemes that is locally of finite type and Cohen-Macaulay, the local dimension of X at x equals the local dimension of Y at y = f(x) plus the dimension of the fibre X_y at x. The retained proof is written out: after shrinking X around x, the flat-finite-presentation CM-fibres lemma gives a constant d such that every fibre has dimension d at every point, so f is flat, locally of finite type and of relative dimension d, and the dimension formula for maps of relative dimension d (Morphisms, rel-dimension-dimension) concludes. Retained author proof at lines 5857-5866.
